questions.text: Is St Helena part of the UK?
questions.explanation: British overseas territories, such as St Helena and the Falkland Islands are linked to the UK but arenot part of it.

questions.text: Where is Theatreland?
questions.explanation: London’s West End, also known as ‘Theatreland’, is particularly well known for its theatres.

questions.text: What is the name of the UK currency?
questions.explanation: The currency in the UK is thepound sterling(symbol £).

questions.explanation: Diwali is often calledthe Festival of Lights.

questions.text: Which two languages combined to become one English language?
questions.explanation: After the Norman Conquest, the king and his noblemen had spokenNorman Frenchand the peasants had continued to speakAnglo-Saxon. Gradually these two languages combined to become one English language.

questions.text: Where did the Spanish Armada come from?
questions.explanation: In 1588 the English defeated the Spanish Armada (a large fleet of ships), which had been sent bySpainto conquer England and restore Catholicism.

questions.text: What is the name of the War Memorial located in Whitehall?

questions.text: The UK government has never suspended the Northern Ireland Assembly.
questions.explanation: False. The Northern Ireland Assembly has been suspended on a few occasions.

questions.text: What kind of church did Scotland establish in 1560?
questions.explanation: In 1560, the predominantly Protestant Scottish Parliament abolished the authority of the Pope in Scotland and Roman Catholic religious services became illegal.A Protestant Churchof Scotland with an elected leadership was established but, unlike in England, this was not a state Church.

questions.text: When was the Domesday Book written?
questions.explanation: William the conqueror sent people all over England to draw up lists of all the towns and villages. The people who lived there, who owned the land and what animals they owned were also listed. This was called the Domesday Book, which gives a picture of society in England justafter the Norman Conquest.

questions.text: The Northern Ireland Assembly cannot make decisions on which two of the following issues?
questions.explanation: The Northern Ireland Assembly can make decisions on issues such as: education, agriculture, the environment health and social services, but it cannot make decisions onimmigration or defenceissues.

questions.text: What should you do to make a complaint about the police (choose two answers)?
questions.explanation: Anyone can make a complaint about the policeby going to a police station and writing to the Chief Constable of the police force involved. Complaints can also be made to an independent body: the Independent Police Complaints Commission in England and Wales, the Police Complaints Commissioner for Scotland or the Police Ombudsman for Northern Ireland.

options.text: Write a complaint letter to the House of Commons
Go to the Police station directly
Write to the Chief Constable of the police force involved

questions.text: What flower did William Wordsworth write about?
questions.explanation: William Wordsworth wrote‘The Daffodils’.

questions.text: When is St Andrew’s day celebrated?
questions.explanation: St Andrew’s day, patron of Scotland, is celebrated on the30th of November.

questions.text: Who was the architect that rebuilt Saint Paul’s cathedral after the Great Fire in 1666?
questions.explanation: In 1666, a great fire destroyed much of the city, including many churches and St Paul’s Cathedral. London was rebuilt with a new St Paul\\\\\\\'s, which was designed by a famous architect,Sir Christopher Wren.

questions.text: When were the first coins in Britain made?
questions.explanation: The people ofthe Iron Agemade the first coins to be minted in Britain.

questions.text: Who was Emmeline Pankhurst?
questions.explanation: Emmeline Pankhurst was born in Manchester in 1858. She set up the women’s Franchise League in 1889, which fought to get the vote in local elections for married women. In 1903 she helped found the Women’s Social and Political Union (WSPU). This was the first group whose members were called‘suffragettes’.

questions.text: Who did Britain fight against in the Crimean War?
questions.explanation: From 1853 to 1856, Britain fought with Turkey and France againstRussiain the Crimean War.

questions.text: How old do you have to be to buy alcohol in the UK?
questions.explanation: It is a criminal offence to sell alcohol to anyone who is under 18 or to buy alcohol for people who are under the age of18. (There is one exception: people aged 16 or over can drink alcohol with a meal in a hotel or restaurant).
